content: At the base of the Griesbachian stage, a significant number of spore species emerge in the fossil record, resulting in an increase in overall diversity. This transition is also characterized by a substantial decline in a specific group of pteridosperm pollen, particularly Vittatina. One species within this group, Lueckisporites virkkiae, remains rare but consistently present in the lower part of the Griesbachian and gradually disappears in the upper part of this stage. The distribution of other groups, such as taeniate and non-taeniate bisaccate gymnosperm pollen (originating from pteridosperms and conifers), does not exhibit any notable changes across this boundary. However, spores and other gymnosperm pollen types show an increase in both diversity and abundance. These changes align with the transition between the Schuchert Dal Formation (Upper Permian) and the Wordie Creek Formation (Griesbachian equivalent). Contrary to the widely held belief that both marine and terrestrial biota experienced a mass extinction event at the Permian-Triassic boundary, the material studied from Norwegian mid-latitudinal sites provides no evidence of widespread destruction of plant ecosystems. The presence of diverse microfloras from the Griesbachian age supports the hypothesis that the climate in this region allowed most plant species to survive the Permian-Triassic boundary event. Data from mid-Norway, along with previous records from East Greenland and the Barents Shelf, challenge the commonly accepted narrative that the earliest Triassic flora was dominated by herbaceous lycopsids, which supposedly invaded devastated terrestrial ecosystems and became the globally dominant group. This perspective requires revision. Peat is defined as a type of soil formed from dead but not fully decayed plant material, typically found in bog areas. It is a brown, soil-like material characteristic of boggy, acidic ground, consisting of partially decomposed vegetable matter. Phycology is the scientific study of algae. Phytomorphology, or plant morphology, is the study of the physical form and external structure of plants. It involves examining the development, form, and structure of plants and interpreting these characteristics based on similarities in their design and origin.
